source_text: Si autem dixeris, quia una est forma baptismatis, qua diversae aetatis homines consecrantur, fateberis etiam me tacente commemorationem ibi nec generationis infectae nec carnis diabolicae nec Adae aliquam contineri; ad quod tamen suo loco, quamvis ad traducem non spectet, plene responsuri sumus.
pass_a_gloss: But if you have said that there is one form of baptism by which humans of diverse age are consecrated, you will confess even with me silent that a commemoration there neither of infected generation nor of diabolical flesh nor of Adam is contained; to which nevertheless in its own place, although it does not look to the vine-layer, we are going to respond fully.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent

pass_b_english: If, however, you say that one form of baptism consecrates people of different ages, you will admit, even if I say nothing, that it contains no mention of infected generation, diabolical flesh, or Adam. Although this does not concern the transmission of sin, we shall nevertheless answer it fully in its own place.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
